breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer banks and consumer-finance firms that outsource loan guarantees should check whether their customers' data passed through the affected system, prepare for phishing and identity-fraud attempts using the leaked licence numbers and income data, and warn affected customers not to trust calls, emails or messages that cite their loan details. The leak of driver's licence numbers together with income and guarantee amounts is directly usable for impersonation and social engineering against bank customers.
breaking.headline: SMBC Consumer Finance discloses breach of up to 321,018 customers' data
breaking.known: SMBC Consumer Finance detected unauthorised access to its loan-guarantee system on 2 November and cut off access the same day; data was sent outside the company. The leaked data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, driver's licence numbers, employer and income details, and guarantee amounts and other contract information. Images of identity documents were not included. The firm provides guarantee services to 189 financial institutions, including regional banks, credit unions and online banks; its own Promise consumer-finance service does not use the affected system and is unaffected. No secondary harm from misuse of the data had been confirmed at the time of disclosure.
breaking.source_name: Nikkei, 5 November 2026; TBS NEWS DIG, 5 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
breaking.summary: SMBC Consumer Finance, the Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group consumer-finance arm, said on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to its loan-guarantee system exposed personal data of up to 321,018 people, including names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, driver's licence numbers, employer details, income and loan guarantee amounts. The intrusion was detected on 2 November and access was cut off the same day; the guarantee system is suspended while checks continue. No misuse of the data has been confirmed so far, and images of identity documents were not included. The data covers customers of 189 partner banks, credit unions and online banks for which the firm provides loan guarantees; its own Promise consumer-finance service was not affected.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: Which of the 189 partner institutions' customers are affected has not been individually confirmed — the firm says it will contact affected people via partner institutions once the scope is pinned down. Whether the intrusion exploited a specific vulnerability, and the attacker's identity, are undisclosed.

breaking.bfsi_impact: A leaked list of 227,216 corporate customer email addresses is ready-made fuel for targeted phishing and business-email compromise impersonating SMBC. Peer banks using third-party email-delivery services should check their own suppliers' exposure, and customers should treat any message citing SMBC business as suspect unless verified through known channels.
breaking.headline: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation confirms 227,216 email addresses leaked via contractor
breaking.known: The leak came through Arara's email-delivery service 'Arara Message', used by the bank. The affected addresses are recipients of bank emails sent 1 July–31 October 2026, mainly corporate customers plus some sole proprietors. No account numbers, balances, PINs or internet-banking IDs or passwords were included. The bank was told of the unauthorised access on 28 October and received confirmation that data had leaked on 2 November. SMBC and SMBC Trust Bank also announced a new information-sharing arrangement with Japan's National Police Agency from 9 November to speed up anti-fraud cooperation.
breaking.source_name: TBS NEWS DIG, 5 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
breaking.summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation said on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to its email-delivery contractor Arara's 'Arara Message' service leaked 227,216 email addresses — the recipients of emails the bank sent between 1 July and 31 October, mainly corporate customers and some sole proprietors. No account numbers, balances, PINs or internet-banking IDs or passwords were included. The bank was told of the unauthorised access on 28 October and received confirmation of the leak on 2 November.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — third-party data breach
breaking.unknown: The cause of the unauthorised access at the contractor and the full extent of any further exposure are still being checked with the contractor. Whether any leaked addresses have been used in phishing has not been reported.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer banks using third-party or supplier-built mobile banking systems should review supplier security settings, account-enumeration controls and verification for non-designated transfers, and check whether any supplier system permits transfers without the customer logging in. APAC banks should watch the regulator's detailed report due 12 November.
breaking.headline: Bank SinoPac confirms hackers exploited supplier flaw in unauthorised transfers
breaking.known: At a press conference on the evening of 4 November, reported by Focus Taiwan (CNA) at 21:01 SGT, the bank said external hackers breached security settings at the supplier of its new online banking transaction system, used trial-and-error to obtain valid accounts sharing an ID-number prefix, and moved funds to a single Taipei Fubon Bank account, which was frozen. The bank said it reimbursed customers on 3 November, found no evidence of personal-data leakage, hired an independent cybersecurity team, shared threat information with peers via F-ISAC, and will seek compensation from the foreign supplier, whose system is used by no other bank in Taiwan. Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission requires a detailed major-incident report by 12 November.
breaking.summary: Taiwan's Bank SinoPac said on 4 November 2026 that external hackers exploited security settings at the supplier of its new mobile banking system, causing 427 unauthorised transfers totalling about NT$41.76 million (about US$1.27 million) on 3 November. The bank has reimbursed affected customers, the single receiving account at another bank was frozen, and the new system has been suspended.
breaking.unknown: The supplier's name, the exact flaw in its security settings, and the attackers' identity are undisclosed, and the case is under criminal investigation. Local reports of the bank's press conference put the affected customer count at 418, against the Financial Supervisory Commission / Focus Taiwan figure of 419 accounts for the same 427 transfers; the wire uses the regulator's figure and flags the one-customer discrepancy.

breaking.bfsi_impact: A named European bank victim with fraudulent transactions: peer banks should review controls on large and exchange-account withdrawals, verify transaction authorisation and suspension procedures, and watch for laundering of any linked funds through exchanges and instant-swap services. Under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act, major ICT incidents carry a short initial reporting window, so EU-regulated peers should check their own incident-classification clocks. Third-party platform access is now a confirmed route in this case: review service-provider platforms that can reach the bank directly, not only customer-facing channels.
breaking.headline: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyberattack enabling fraudulent transactions
breaking.known: The bank's own statement, reported by CoinDesk, Bloomberg and Ledger Insights on 4 November, confirms the attack and the fraudulent transactions. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT first flagged a suspected loss of more than $106 million at an unnamed EU entity on 2 November and named Arkéa on 3 November, putting the total above $133 million; Bitquery traced $108.8 million in USDC withdrawals from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX accounts over 1–2 November, and Crypto.com said it blocked funds linked to the incident. In a further statement on the evening of 4 November, reported by AFP/Reuters and updated by CNA at 00:57 SGT on 5 November, the bank said attackers reached Arkéa directly through the platform of one of its service providers — not through Fortuneo, and not through client accounts — used the bank's own account to transfer funds to other banks, and then converted funds into cryptocurrency via specialist platforms; a portion of funds was blocked and recovery efforts are under way. The bank gave a provisional estimate of about €100 million, validated the order of magnitude of the reported $133 million (about €118 million) figure, but has not confirmed a final figure. The Paris public prosecutor's office has opened an investigation into an attack on an automated data processing system by an organised group. On 5 November the bank said nearly all operations had resumed after security checks and additional safeguards, customer funds were unaffected, and the losses were lower than the $133 million figure reported in the press and not of a nature to undermine the group's financial strength.
breaking.source_name: Reuters / AFP via CNA, 4-5 November 2026; Cointelegraph, 5 November 2026
breaking.summary: French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed on 4 November 2026 that it was the target of a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions. The bank says the incident is now under control, some transactions were temporarily suspended, regulators and supervisory authorities have been notified, and clients face no financial consequences. In its evening update the bank gave a provisional estimate of about €100 million, with the final figure still being assessed.
breaking.unknown: The bank has not confirmed a final amount, the attack method, which service provider's platform was used, whether the provider itself was breached (reported by Le Figaro, not confirmed by the bank), or how much, if anything, has been recovered. The $133 million figure is the investigator's estimate, repeated in the press, not a bank-confirmed loss; the bank has validated only its order of magnitude.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks, payment aggregators and fintech partners with Indian operations or Indian payment-API exposure should check API inventories, shut down dormant or test interfaces, enforce beneficiary verification and cooling periods, and flag ₹1-scale test transfers to new beneficiaries followed by larger transfers. ARTEX is already tracked in the Storm-0940/ARTEX deep-research page.
entries.headline: CERT-In warns India's BFSI sector of escalating AI-driven ‘Crafty Falcon’ payment-API attacks
entries.known: The advisory, issued 4 November and reported widely on 5 November, updates CERT-In's 9 October advisory on payment and disbursement API abuse. CERT-In's CSIRT-Fin says successful attacks continue to be reported, including by NBFCs and fintech firms that had already received earlier restricted advisories and taken remedial measures, and that remediated entities have been deliberately re-targeted after incomplete remediation. Attackers use publicly available AI-driven tools — ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI — to survey targets, generate tailored attack scripts and execute full attack chains at machine speed, invoking victims' own payment and disbursement APIs to move funds to mule accounts, after testing routes with micro-value transactions as small as ₹1. Merchant settlement APIs were abused and cryptocurrency wallet keys stolen. Attacks were timed to coincide with weekends and public holidays. CERT-In advised 24x7 monitoring, API inventories with dormant interfaces shut down, beneficiary-name verification and cooling periods for new beneficiaries.
entries.source_name: Indian Express, 5 November 2026; PTI via Rediff, 4 November 2026
entries.summary: India's CERT-In issued an advisory on 4 November 2026 naming the AI-assisted threat actor CRAFTY FALCON and warning that attacks abusing banks', NBFCs' and fintech firms' own payment and disbursement APIs for unauthorised fund transfers are active, ongoing and escalating.
entries.unknown: No individual victim institution was named in the public reporting of the advisory, and no aggregate loss figure for the current escalation was published. Whether any affected entity is a bank with Singapore or APAC operations beyond India is not stated.

entries.bfsi_impact: APAC banks and firms with Korean operations should watch the FSC inspection programme and the planned CEO-accountability measures; the wave shows small virtual-asset and electronic-payment firms are the weakest link, and leaked personal data may feed voice-phishing against bank customers.
entries.headline: South Korea regulator discloses 40 breaches at 37 financial firms; sector-wide inspections ordered
entries.known: The Financial Services Commission announced the measures on 5 November at an industry-wide forum chaired by Chairman Lee Eok-won, attended by the Financial Supervisory Service and the Korea Financial Security Institute. No individual users have yet suffered direct financial losses, and no account passwords that could enable fraudulent transactions were confirmed among the leaked data. The FSC will inspect about 580 financial entities by year-end, plans to lift network-separation rules, launch an AI-based security framework, and draft a Digital Finance Safety Act by the first quarter of 2027. The incidents include previously reported breaches at brokerages, insurers and virtual-asset firms.
entries.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission said 40 cybersecurity incidents were reported at 37 financial firms between 30 September and 5 November 2026, exposing about 473,000 records, with about ₩1 billion (about US$746,000) stolen from company-managed funds at some electronic financial service providers, virtual asset businesses and P2P lenders.
entries.unknown: The FSC has not named all 37 firms or broken down the 40 incidents by firm, and whether any leaked data is exploited in secondary crime such as voice phishing remains unconfirmed.

entries.bfsi_impact: Open banking / API deployments using affected WSO2 versions should confirm patching before the deadline.
entries.headline: WSO2 Open Banking CVE-2025-11969 — KEV deadline 5 November
entries.known: Listed in CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities with a 5 November remediation deadline, as reported in the 4 November brief.
entries.summary: Deadline watch carried from the 4 November daily brief. Not a new breaking item on 4 November itself.
entries.unknown: Whether affected BFSI deployments have completed remediation by the deadline — no compliance outcome was published in the brief.

entries.bfsi_impact: WordPress estates, including marketing and customer-facing sites run by financial firms, should patch before the deadline.
entries.headline: WordPress CVE-2026-119977 — KEV deadline 6 November
entries.known: The only new KEV entry in the 4 November brief, with a Friday 6 November deadline; patch to 7.1.4, as reported in the brief.
entries.summary: Deadline watch carried from the 4 November daily brief. Not a new breaking item on 4 November itself.
entries.unknown: No successful compromise via this race was publicly confirmed in the brief.
